newsitem.title: MALTA: Air Malta makes core operations losses in year.
newsitem.headline: Air Malta makes core operations losses in year.

text.p: State-owned Air Malta made a loss of 1 million Maltese pounds ($2.7 million) on its core operations in the financial year that ended last March and is expected to lose 4.2 million Maltese pounds from core operations in the current financial year, Prime Minister Alfred Sant said late on Friday.

"Excluding certain exceptional gains and income earned from subsidiaries, mainly on duty-free operations, Air Malta made a loss of 1 million Maltese pounds in the year ending in March 1996," Sant told the Maltese parliament, quoting the airline's auditors, Coopers and Lybrand.

"This loss was in effect incurred on Air Malta's core airline activities. A significantly larger loss, amounting to 4.2 million Maltese pounds, is forecast by the company in its core operations in the year ending March 31, 1997," he added.
Sant did not give reasons for the airline's losses, the first since the airline was set up in 1975.

Air Malta was negatively affected in 1996 by a six percent drop in tourist arrivals to Malta, which clashed with heavy investment by the airline in the purchase of regional aircraft and the opening of new routes to create a hub network in the Mediterranean.
The airline also took a 49-percent stake in a new Italian airline, AzzuraAir, based in Bergamo, which started operations in December.

The airline did not issue its annual report in 1996 because its publication clashed with the general elections in October. Airline chairman Joe N. Tabone resigned immediately the new Labour government was elected.
